name: Eachanari Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple about 12 km from Coimbatore city on the Palakkad road, known for its very large stone image of Vinayagar and administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Local tradition says the huge Vinayagar image was being carted from Madurai to the Perur Pateeswarar Temple when the cart's axle broke here, and the deity was installed on the spot.

name: Tiruneelakkudi Neelakandeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the Kaveri in Thanjavur district counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, praised in the Tevaram hymns of the Nayanar saints Tirunavukkarasar and Sambandar. Its lingam is unusual, with square projections and a rough surface.
story: The name recalls the churning of the ocean of milk: Shiva swallowed the poison, Parvati held his throat to make him Neelakanta, and she then soothed him with oil here, a rite the temple still performs.

name: Panamukkumpally Sastha Temple
significance: A Sastha temple in Thrissur city that takes part every year in the Thrissur Pooram, the state's best-known temple festival.

name: Mukthi Natheshwara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Binnamangala near Nelamangala outside Bengaluru, which the article dates to the Chola period around 1110 CE.

name: Pazhoor Perumthrikkovil
significance: A 12th-century sandhara-type Kerala temple with doors on all four sides, a granite plinth and a circular vimana, protected by the Kerala State Archaeology Department since 1994 and notable for its old woodwork and murals of Puranic scenes.

name: Palayoor Mahadeva Temple
significance: An ancient Shiva temple site at Palayoor near Chavakkad; the temple no longer stands, the site having been converted into a Christian church in the traditional account of St Thomas's arrival in Malabar.
story: It is counted among the 108 Shiva temples said to have been founded by Parasurama, who is held to have installed the deity himself.

name: Kilimarathukavu Temple
builtDisplay: present temple rebuilt in the 21st c.
significance: A Shiva-Parvati temple at Kadakkal that also houses Dharma Sastha and Ayyappan; the original structure was destroyed and the present temple built in the 21st century, with the Travancore Devaswom Board taking over administration in 2011.
story: Temple lore holds that Shiva and Parvati came here disguised as forest dwellers to test Arjuna, and that Shiva revealed himself, granted him the Pashupatastra and then remained on the spot as a lingam.

name: Bhimeswar Dham
significance: A Shiva shrine on Dakini Hill about 13 km from Guwahati where a hill stream runs continuously over the lingam; devotees hold it to be one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, an identification scholars dispute. Maha Shivaratri is its principal observance.
story: The Shiva Purana account told here has Shiva destroying the demon Bhimasura when he attacked King Priyadharman at worship, the stream over the lingam being Shiva's perspiration from that fight.

name: Thirumalida Swayambhoo Shiva Temple
significance: A swayambhu Shiva temple on the bank of the Manimala river at Mallappally, described as the only west-facing swayambhu Shiva shrine in Kerala; Maha Shivaratri draws thousands of pilgrims.

name: Ashtamsa Varadha Anjaneyar Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple at Peelamedu in Coimbatore completed in 2004, whose salagrama-stone west-facing image shows Lakshmi in the deity's right palm and is dressed in a different alankaram each day.

name: Lakshminarasimha Temple, Vignasante
deity: Narasimha, with Venugopala and Lakshmi Narayana
significance: A soapstone trikuta temple of about 1286 CE with a three-storey Vesara vimana, built by the brothers Appayya, Gopala and Madhava under Hoysala king Narasimha III; it is one of the last Hoysala temples raised before the Delhi Sultanate invasions, and is an ASI-protected monument.

name: Veerateeswarar Temple, Thirukovilur
significance: A 10th-century Chola temple on the Then Pennai river at Thirukoilur, built as two parallel enclosures each with a three-tiered rajagopuram. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by three Nayanmars in the Tevaram and one of the Ashta Veerattanam shrines marking Shiva's eight victories over demons.

name: Karpaka Vinayakar Temple
significance: A rock-cut cave shrine at Pillayarpatti holding carvings of Ganesha, a Shiva lingam and a figure read as Ardhanarishvara or Harihara, attributed to about 650 CE and enlarged with mandapams in later centuries. It is one of the nine ancestral temples of the Nagarathar (Chettiar) community, and 11th-century panchaloha images were recovered during 19th-century restoration.

name: Masilamaniswara Temple, Thirumullaivoyal
significance: A 9th-century Chola foundation near Chennai, extended by later Cholas, Pandyas and the Vijayanagara rulers, with an unusual Gaja Prishtam (elephant-back) vimana. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram and belongs to the Shakti triad of Tondaimandalam.
story: The temple's tradition tells of King Thondaiman striking a lingam hidden in dense mullai thickets during a campaign; Shiva and Parvati appeared, helped him defeat two brothers, and he raised the temple on the spot.

name: Akshayapureeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Akshayapureeswarar), with a principal shrine to Shani
significance: A 13th-century Shiva temple whose inscriptions credit Parakrama Pandyan I, best known as one of the 27 Nakshatra temples of Tamil Nadu, linked to the Pushya asterism and holding a Shani shrine with his consorts Jyestha and Mandha.
story: The legend here has Shani, lamed by Yama, tripping over the roots of a vila tree at this spot on Akshaya Tritiya, whereupon Shiva appeared as Akshayapureeswarar, healed him and blessed him with marriage.

name: Bata Mangala Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine on the Jagannath Sadak about 7 km from Puri, where pilgrims customarily stop to pray to the goddess before continuing to the Jagannath Temple.
story: It is told that when Brahma stood bewildered before the void, Bata Mangala appeared and directed him to Jagannath, allowing creation to begin.

name: Bharat Mata Mandir
deity: Bharat Mata (the nation personified as a goddess)
significance: A temple on the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith campus founded by Babu Shiv Prasad Gupta and inaugurated in 1936, which holds no image at all: its object of veneration is a to-scale marble relief map of undivided India. Gandhi opened it, remarking that the only thing enshrined there was the map.

name: Kolanjiappar Temple
significance: A Murugan temple on the outskirts of Virudhachalam with a five-tiered rajagopuram, pillared hall and sanctum, administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department; Panguni Uthiram, a ten-day Vasantha Utsavam and the Adi festival are its main celebrations.
story: Tradition holds that Shiva sent his son Murugan as a hunter into the Kolanji forest to test the saint Sundarar, and that Murugan afterwards settled there as Kolanjiappar; another account says a cow was found mysteriously giving milk beneath a kolanji bush at the site.

name: Thalakodu Sree Krishna Temple
significance: An old Krishna temple at Cheriyoor near Taliparamba in north Kerala, belonging to the Mullappally illam and open to all Hindus.

name: Pallikonda Perumal Temple, Malayadippatti
deity: Vishnu (Pallikonda Perumal, reclining), with Mahalakshmi and Bhudevi
significance: A rock-cut cave temple about 33 km from Pudukkottai, dated by its inscriptions to the 7th–8th century and housing a reclining Vishnu; it is paired at the same site with a Shiva cave temple and is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. Its dvarapalas are unusual in having only two arms.
story: The sage Dhivakara Maharishi is said to have done penance here for Vishnu's grace, and the deity, called Kan Thirantha Perumal, is believed to cure ailments of the eyes.

name: Amaravila Rameswaram Sri Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about a kilometre from Neyyattinkara whose sreekovil holds an east-facing lingam together with a west-facing Parvati; Maha Shivaratri with its Pongala offering and a ten-day festival in December–January are the main observances.
story: The temple's name comes from the belief that Rama himself installed the image here, and it is counted among the 108 Shiva temples ascribed to the sage Parasurama.

name: Kaalikaamba Kamatheshwara Temple
significance: A temple in the old Nagarathpet quarter of Bengaluru dedicated jointly to Kaalikaamba and Kamatheshwara, described as roughly eight centuries old and dating to the Chola period.

name: Kashi Vishweshwar Temple, Kadugodi
builtDisplay: Chola period, reign of Rajendra Chola
significance: A Chola-period Shiva temple in Kadugodi on the eastern edge of Bengaluru, assigned to the reign of Rajendra Chola and showing design carried over from the earlier Western Ganga dynasty. The locality's name comes from the temple standing in forest — kadu (forest) and gudi (temple) — and the original lingam, once stolen, was replaced with one brought from Varanasi.

name: Thirukolakka Sapthapureeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Sapthapureeswarar), with consort Osai Kodutha Nayaki
significance: A Shiva temple at Keezhai Thirukolakka, historically called Sapthapuri, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and sung in the Tevaram by Tirugnanasambandar and Sundarar.
story: It is at this shrine that the child saint Sambandar is said to have miraculously received his golden cymbals.

name: Eshwara Temple, Kengeri
significance: An 11th-century Shiva temple at Kengeri assigned to the reign of Rajendra Chola I, one of the small group of Chola-era shrines surviving in the Bengaluru area; it stands close to the Kote Anjaneya Swamy Temple.

name: Tirunaarayur Soundaryeswarar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, sung by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram; the temple is known for a swayambhu Ganesha worshipped as Polla Pillaiyar.
story: Tradition holds that the deity revealed himself here to the boy Nambiyandar Nambi, sent by his father to make the ritual offerings.

name: Mathur Shiva Temple
deity: Shiva, with Parvati in the same sanctum
significance: One of the 108 celebrated Shiva temples of Kerala, at Kunnamkulam, where the west-facing Shiva shares the sanctum with an east-facing Parvati and the lingam is held to be an unshaped reddish rudrakshasila. Maha Shivaratri is the chief festival.
story: The image is said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Maragathambikai Chandrachoodesvarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Chandra Choodeswarar), with Parvati as Maragathambal
significance: A hill temple at Hosur with 13th-century inscriptions, credited to the Hoysala chief Thirupuvanamalla Barvatharaja Anthiyazhvar around 1260 and enlarged under the Cholas, Hoysalas and Vijayanagara rulers; the surrounding region is treated in the Bhadragiri Mahatmyam of the Brahmanda Purana.

name: Thirumanangeeswarar Temple
deity: Thiruvudai Amman (chief goddess), with Shiva as Thirumanangeeswarar
significance: A goddess-led Shiva temple near Minjur north of Chennai, forming with the Kodiyidai Amman temple at Thirumullaivoyal and the Vadivudai Amman temple at Tiruvottiyur the Shakti triad of Tondaimandalam.

name: Arakeshvara Temple, Hole Alur
significance: A mid-10th-century temple raised by the Western Ganga king Butuga II to mark his defeat of the Cholas at the Battle of Takkolam, with a plain plan of sanctum, vestibule, closed hall and detached open mantapa. Its rounded pillars carry bas-reliefs of that victory over the Chola prince Rajaditya. It is a monument of national importance under the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Bhairavakona
deity: Shiva in eight forms (Shashinaga, Rudra, Visweswara, Nagarikeswara, Bhargeswara, Rameswara, Mallikarjuna and Pakshamalika), with a separate Kala Bhairava shrine
significance: A group of eight inscribed rock-cut cave shrines cut from a single formation in the Nallamala Hills, dated to the 7th–8th century and compared with the rock-cut work at Mahabalipuram; each cave carries a Brahma-Vishnu-Shiva grouping, alongside life-size dvarapalas, carved lions and Harihara figures, with a 200 m waterfall beside the site. Mahasivaratri and Kartika Purnima draw large pilgrim crowds.
story: Local tradition traces the name to a shepherd, Kalabhairava Kondayya, who made a vow to the deity during a drought.

name: Someshwara Swamy Temple
significance: A Chola-period Shiva temple at Agara on Sarjapura Road in Bengaluru, described in the article as roughly 1,200 years old.

name: Nagore Naganathaswamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Nagore with a rajagopuram and an inner prakaram carrying shrines to Rahu, Dakshinamurti, Vinayaka and Murugan; it is one of the serpent-associated Shiva shrines of the Kaveri delta, and Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham and Karthika Deepam are observed here.
story: The sthala purana holds that Vasuki and other sacred serpents came to worship at this and three other snake temples, and that the deity appeared here as a self-manifested lingam beneath a punnai tree; townspeople say snakes do not bite anyone in Nagore.

name: Sri Pandi Muneeswarar Temple
deity: Pandi Muneeswarar, identified with the Pandya king Nedunchezhiyan
significance: A folk-deity temple at Melamadai in Madurai, popularly known as Pandi Kovil, still maintained by descendants of the Muthuraiyar family who founded it.
story: It is said that Valliammal and Periyasamy unearthed an image eight feet down near Mattuthavani after a bearded sage appeared in a dream declaring himself Pandyan Nedunchezhiyan, doing penance for the injustice done to Kovalan; the temple was raised where the image was found.

name: Patcheeswarar Temple
significance: A Pallava-period Shiva temple at Cheyyar with an east-facing five-tiered rajagopuram, a sanctum with antarala and maha mandapam, a Nataraja Sabha holding bronzes, and shrines to Parvati, Vinayaka, Murugan, Garuda, Gajalakshmi and the Nalvar.
story: The name is explained by the tradition that Garuda, the eagle mount of Vishnu, worshipped Shiva at this spot.

name: Betrayaswamy Temple
deity: Vishnu (Betrayaswamy / Devaperumal), with Lakshmi as Soundaryavalli
significance: A Vishnu temple at Denkanikottai in the Tamil Nadu-Karnataka border country, built in the Hoysala idiom with a five-tiered rajagopuram; the Wodeyars of Mysore endowed its major shrines and pillared halls in the 16th century.
story: The Skanda Purana account here has Venkateswara appearing to the sage Kanva to save him from the yaksha Devandagadagan, taking the form of a hunter and killing the yaksha with a mace called Denkani, from which the town takes its name.

name: Kothandaramar Temple, Thillaivilagam
deity: Rama (Kothandaramar), with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman
significance: One of the five Pancha Rama Kshetrams of Tiruvarur district and among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnava tradition, noted for a four-foot standing Hanuman and for fine carving on the image of Rama.

name: Kollam Rameswaram Mahadeva Temple
significance: A 12th-century Shiva temple at Thangassery attributed to an order of the Chera ruler Rama Kulasekhara, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala; it has a rectangular sanctum with stone and wood carving, a copper flagstaff, two towers and two recorded inscriptions.
story: The sage Parasurama is held in tradition to be its founder.

name: Talupulamma Temple, Lova
significance: A grama-devata shrine set in a valley between the forested hills of Darakonda and Teegakonda near Tuni, worshipped as a goddess who grants wishes and following the Grama Devata agamas; its fifteen-day Jatara in Chaitra and the Ashada month utsavams draw large crowds.

name: Panchavan Madeviyar Pallippadai Temple
significance: A rare Chola pallippadai, a temple raised over a burial: Rajendra Chola placed the ashes of his stepmother Panchavan Madeviyar, a queen of Rajaraja I, in an urn here and built a Shiva shrine above it, the urn still shown over the lingam. It fell into ruin and was restored by the Tamil Nadu Archaeology Department in 1978.

name: Kondazhy Thrithamthali Siva-Parvathy Temple
significance: One of the 108 celebrated Shiva temples of Kerala, which under Chera rule served as the central temple for the administration of the surrounding eighteen tiers; besides the Parvati shrine it holds eleven subsidiary deities. Its sculpture was damaged during Tipu Sultan's invasion of Kerala and stayed so for about two centuries.
story: Tradition credits the sage Parashurama with installing the Shiva image on the south bank of the Nila.

name: Kamaleswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Pudupet neighbourhood of Chennai, best known for its association with the 18th-century dubash and philanthropist Pachaiyappa Mudaliar.

name: Nattatreeswarar Temple
significance: A 10th-century Chola temple standing on a hillock island in the Kaveri on the Erode-Karur road, with an athi tree in the precinct held to be about 3,000 years old; Aadi Perukku and the Tamil New Year draw thousands of pilgrims.
story: Temple lore says the sage Agastya raised a lingam of sand on the hillock and meditated there, and that Shiva appeared and declared the place would bless not only the sage but all his devotees.

name: Singamadai Ayyanar Temple, Nalli
deity: Ayyanar (Singamadai Ayyanar), with consorts Purana and Pushkala
significance: An Ayyanar temple beside Singamadai lake about 18 km from Sattur, built by the Sevalpatti zamindar roughly five centuries ago; it also houses Pechiyamman and several forms of Karuppasamy, and its Masi-month Shivaratri festival draws people from some thirty villages around.
story: It is told that a devotee carrying sacred sand from Srivilliputtur during a drought set it down near Nalli when floods threatened the village, and a voice from the sky declared that Ayyanar had saved the land and crops and would bless the people if a temple were raised for him.
